text: Five is our starting mix. A reader pilot will establish each game’s contribution.

The five formats have distinct jobs within the publisher’s daily experience. Shabd offers word curiosity and meaning; Jodi explains relationships; Over adds cricket participation; Niti carries a thought into conversation; Nishana provides a familiar personal challenge. The shared home and progress connect choices. These intended contributions explain the starting collection, not a proven optimum or evidence of cross-game conversion. Reader testing should establish each contribution.
Sources: supplied design rationale, organizer brief pp. 7, 9, 11, 13–17, and prototype shared home/progression.

text: Pilot test: voluntary return, useful article engagement and manageable editorial effort.

The proposed engagement system combines a satisfying payoff, a fresh invitation and depth through mastery and continuity. These are hypotheses to test rather than forecasts. The prototype currently has authored selectable editions, personal results, Niti cards and shared participation history/levels. Future production work includes checked daily/current publishing, deeper challenge variation and hosted share invitations. A reader may choose a different game on another day while retaining the same home and participation history. This does not demonstrate actual cross-game return behavior.
Pilot question: compare voluntary return days and meaningful article engagement with the ordinary news journey, while monitoring completion, clarity and editorial effort.
Sources: supplied organizer brief p. 9, design rationale, src/systems/progression.js and Doc/Mashal journey.md.

Closing: ordinary habits gave us the starting points. One daily destination gives those interests a short, approachable moment of participation. Reporting supplies context and meaning where useful. Niti can carry a thought into a conversation, while Nishana offers familiar skill play. The five choices form one submission concept. The benefits should earn validation with readers. A brief prototype demonstration can follow this close.
